xBRIEFInfo.description: Project definition -- synthesized gestalt of the project

narratives.Overview:
ViLM (Video Library Manager) is a native macOS and iOS application for indexing, reviewing and organising a personal library of local video files. It recursively scans folders into an embedded SQLite catalogue stored alongside the media itself, and manages a metadata graph over that library: video assets, actor/entity profiles (with aliases and photo galleries), tags, series and episodes, playlists, and saved smart collections. On top of that it provides playback with a pop-out player, 4x4 contact-sheet frame navigation, duplicate detection, bulk file renaming, and a review workflow.

It is general-purpose video library management -- not tied to any particular kind of content. Design priorities, in order: the user's data is never silently lost or altered; the library is fully local and offline; the app stays responsive on device.

Solo project, public repository, single maintainer. The Human Operator reviews and commits all work himself through Xcode's source control; agents prepare work and hand it back rather than committing.
narratives.tech stack:
Swift and SwiftUI, targeting macOS 14+ and iOS 17+.

- Persistence: SQLite via GRDB.swift, with an ordered schema-migration chain in LibraryStore.
- Media: AVFoundation / AVKit for playback, frame extraction, metadata and transcoding.
- Packaging: Xcode project (ViLM.xcodeproj) for the app; Swift Package Manager for the LibraryCore domain package.
- Tests: XCTest, concentrated in LibraryCore/Tests/LibraryCoreTests (~22 suites). Run with
  `swift test --package-path LibraryCore`.
- No CI pipeline. Verification is local test runs plus validation on a physical device.

Deliberately minimal third-party surface: GRDB is effectively the only runtime dependency.
narratives.Architecture:
Two layers, split so the domain logic is testable without a UI or a simulator:

1. ViLM/ViLM/ -- the SwiftUI application. Views, navigation, and view-local state.
2. LibraryCore/ -- a pure, dependency-light Swift package holding persistence and domain services. This is where the test suite lives and where new runtime logic belongs.

Key seams:
- LibrarySession -- central runtime state: active library, search/filter criteria, selection. Also   supports federation, where several libraries are attached at once.
- LibraryStore -- the single GRDB connection per library, owning migrations, transactions and   relative-path resolution. Data lives in a .catalog directory beside the video files, so a library   is portable: relative paths plus stable UUIDs.
- Domain services -- LibraryScanner, ContactSheetService, VideoDuplicateAnalyzer, VideoEditingService,   FileRenamerService, LibraryBackupService, LibraryFederation, ActorSync. Each is independently testable.

Deliberate constraint worth knowing: the assets table stores identity and user-authored metadata only. File size, duration, dimensions and codec are NOT persisted -- they are read from the filesystem and AVFoundation on demand. This is the root of performance findings F5 and F6; the iOS Performance & Battery Optimization spec adds those columns in its Phase 3.
narratives.RisksAndUnknowns:
The persistence core is structurally sound -- one shared connection per library, WAL, foreign keys, per-call transactions -- and the riskiest single-file operations correctly follow copy, verify, replace. The real risk sits at the SEAMS. Five systemic patterns, from the project's own defect inventory:

1. Database and filesystem writes are non-atomic and inconsistently ordered. Deletes remove the row    before the file; renames move the file before the row; profile-photo renames happen after the    transaction with swallowed errors. Each ordering has a failure mode that loses metadata or orphans files.
2. `try?` on persistence calls inside write paths conflates a FAILED READ with an EMPTY RESULT, after    which a full-row save destroys data. This exact bug class has been found and fixed three times.
3. Operation lifetime is tied to view lifetime. Long-running detached tasks keep running after their    view is gone, while onDisappear revokes the security scopes they depend on.
4. Batch mutations run as N independent transactions, so one mid-loop error leaves partial state.
5. 'File exists, so skip' caching without content-aware invalidation, which silently defeats regeneration.

Treat any change touching a database/filesystem seam as high blast radius, and prefer wrapping batch work in a single transaction.

Open unknowns:
- No performance baseline has ever been captured, so energy and memory claims are currently unfalsifiable.   Establishing one is the blocking Phase 0 of the active performance epic.
- Behaviour on low-RAM devices is untested; bitmap caches are sized with fixed absolute limits.
- Documentation drift is real: the application charter previously described database columns that do not   exist. Verify claims against the source before relying on them.
narratives.Configuration:
Repository layout: the git root is the NESTED directory ~/Development/ViLM/ViLM. The folder one level above it is an untracked workspace holding plans/, BACKLOG.md, DEFECT_INVENTORY.md and TEST_QUALITY_AUDIT.md. Running git one level up reports 'not a git repository'.

Build and test:
- App: open ViLM.xcodeproj in Xcode; targets macOS 14+ and iOS 17+.
- Domain tests: `swift test --package-path LibraryCore`.
- Device validation on a physical iPhone is REQUIRED before merge -- simulator results are not evidence   for layout or energy claims.

Working conventions:
- Characterization tests before refactoring legacy code; never mix a behaviour change into a refactor commit.
- Preserve existing defaults when adding seams for testability.
- Commits are made by the Human Operator in Xcode, directly to main. Branch protection is intentionally   OFF (plan.policy.allowDirectCommitsToMaster=true) to match that workflow. Agents do not commit or push.
- Specifications are authored in Notion and synced to docs/specs/ by notion-sync; they are the source of   truth for requirements. Do not edit generated files locally.
- Directive and GitNexus tooling is installed but gitignored, so this public repo stays free of agent   tooling. Consequence: xbrief/ work state is local-only and not versioned.
